rationale:
Evidence: iteration 1 (base_speed 1.2, kp 4, ki 0.2, kd 0.6, mass 0.6) finished 13 of 20 oval trials, so the change of direction was right, but every s-bend and slalom trial still ended off track at progress 0.11 to 0.22. Max error (0.061 to 0.066) crossed the off-track limit of 0.06 m (body_width 0.18 is already the maximum, so the limit cannot be widened further). RMS error (0.03) and steering oscillation (0.15 to 0.21) are small, so the robot is not oscillating. It is being carried outward on bends, and the line leaves the 3-sensor-wide array (line_loss 1.2 to 1.75 per run). Oval completion is good, so the design is close on gentle curves. The failures on sharp bends point to two causes. First, the sensor array (x within +/-0.03) is too narrow to keep the tape under it when the robot is 3 to 5 cm off-line on a sharp bend, so the signal drops out. Second, the turn rate (wheel_track 0.12) and the speed of 1.2 are too slow to get back onto the tape in time.

Changes: (1) Widen the sensor array to x = -0.04, -0.02, 0, 0.02, 0.04 with 16 mm footprints. The 20 mm spacing leaves no gap, and the wider span keeps the tape in view further out. (2) Reduce wheel_track 0.12 -> 0.10 so the same wheel-speed difference gives a faster turn rate. (3) Lower base_speed 1.2 -> 1.0 to give the controller time to correct on sharp bends. This costs finish time; the oval is the track that must still complete within 3 s, so this is a trade-off I accept while I learn whether the bends are speed-limited. (4) Raise kp 4.0 -> 5.0 for a stronger correction. (5) Keep ki 0.2 for the motor mismatch and kd 0.8 to damp the higher kp. (6) Keep mass 0.6, body width 0.18, and last_direction line-loss handling, which the oval results support.

Expected result: fewer line-loss events and more progress on s-bend and slalom (target progress above 0.5). Oval completion should hold, with finish time possibly near 2 to 2.5 s. Hypotheses: (H1) the wider array reduces line-loss events; (H2) the lower wheel_track gives a faster turn and reduces max_error; (H3) if steering_oscillation rises above 0.5, kp is too high and should drop to about 4. Measurements next: per-track progress, line_loss_events, max_error against the 0.06 limit, and completion_time on the oval.
